newsitem.title: EGYPT: PLO official sees Israel policies leading to war.
newsitem.headline: PLO official sees Israel policies leading to war.

text.p: Senior Palestinian official Farouk Kaddoumi said on Tuesday Israel was unwilling to make peace with the Palestinians and that the policies of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu would lead to war in the Middle East.

"Netanyahu's practices are going to lead to a new war in the region and to more tension," Kaddoumi, the hardline head of the PLO's political (foreign affairs) department, told reporters at Cairo airport.
"Israel does not want to make peace...all it wants is to give the Palestinians control over some aspects but it totally rejects withdrawing out of occupied Arab lands," he added.

Palestinians and Israel agreed in a 1991 Madrid peace conference on the principle of handing over occupied Arab lands for peace but Netanyahu, who was elected last May, has said he refuses to abide by this formula.

Palestinian-Israeli peace talks became paralysed after Netanyahu ordered the construction of a new Jewish settlement in the Arab eastern quarter of Jerusalem which was captured by Israel during a 1967 war.
Both sides blame each other for the impasse which intensive lobbying by the United States, sponsor of the talks, has failed to lift.
Israel regards Jerusalem as its indivisible capital while the Palestinians want the Jewish state to withdraw from the city's eastern part which they want as the capital of their future state.
Netanyahu has come under severe international criticism for lifting a ban on settlements imposed by the former government.

He has also refused to bow to pressure from the United States, Israel's main ally, to curb the settlement building and on Tuesday denied a U.S. report that more than a quarter of the homes were empty.
